newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton output seen at 12.5 mln bales.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton output seen at 12.5 mln bales.

text.p: A Pakistan cotton industry body said on Tuesday that the 1996/97 cotton crop should soar to 12.5 million 375-lb bales, a leap of more than 25 percent over the previous year.
The forecast by the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) was its most optimistic yet for the 1996/97 crop year (July-June). In 1995/96 the cotton crop was 9.94 million bales.

"We will have an exportable surplus of four million bales after meeting the domestic textile needs of 8.5 million bales," Omar Farooq Ehsan Chhani, vice-chairman of the cotton spinners association, told Reuters.

"The main reason for the expected higher production is sowing of cottonseed on 10 million acres (4.1 million hectares) for the 1996/97 crop, up from nine million in 1995/96," he said by telephone from Kot Addu in the Punjab cotton belt.
Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar said last week that Pakistan would have a bumper cotton crop of more than 10 million bales in 1996/97, but gave no detailed estimate.
Maqbool Sadiq, chairman of the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA), said he expected a crop of 10.5 million to 11 million bales despite recent flood damage.
The government has set a target of 10 million bales after last year's crop exceeded a target of 9.5 million bales.
Chhani said higher domestic cotton prices had encouraged farmers to expand the acreage under cotton.
Fine quality cotton rose to more than 2,500 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) at the end of 1995/96 from about 2,400 rupees early in the year, according to rates quoted by the KCA.
Prices touched a high of 2,865 rupees, including a new 10 percent sales tax, on August 11 on demand from spinners for the fine quality cotton, KCA broker Nasim Usman said.
The KCA spot rate for NIAB-78 variety closed 17 rupees up at 2,717 on Tuesday, due to slow supplies from rain-affected farms.

Chhani said complaints from textile mills about excessive exports of raw cotton were unfounded and he brushed aside the impact of recent floods, reported to have destroyed at least 100,000 bales of cotton on farms in Punjab province.

Usman said this week there had been reports of damage to more than 100,000 bales worth one billion rupees ($28 million). An official report said the floods had ruined about 75,000 bales. ($1 = 35.70 rupees)
